Subject: Re: URGENT: Acme Payments — dedicated pool saturation, routing failures (investigating)

Evelyn / team —

Initial triage (09:20–09:30):
- Observed sustained queue depth increase on the acme-prod dedicated pool. Follower pools showed normal behavior.
- Autoscaler engaged but reported insufficient cold-start headroom due to pinned reservations on several priority tenants; several pods timed out during startup.
- NVidia metrics show a sudden spike in GPU compute stalls (kernel queuing) coincident with a spike in long-sequence requests from acme (70–120 tokens avg).
- Error pattern: 503s from the serving runtime indicating request queue overflow; not an application-level model OOM.

Immediate mitigation steps taken (applied at 09:28):
1) Evicted opportunistic workloads from the impacted GPU pool (non-prod & <critical) to free GPU slots.
2) Temporarily increased burst limit for acme's reservation by 25% (emergency override); monitoring effect.
3) Enabled fallback routing to a lower-cost model variant (quantized) for non-critical embedding routes — this reduces quality but preserves throughput.
4) Disabled background maintenance tasks on the cluster to free cycles.

Observing metrics now: queue depth dropping slowly; 5xx rate decreased ~40% since mitigation but still above baseline. Next steps:
- If queueing doesn't resolve to within 5 minutes, we should authorize emergency GPU capacity (cloud burst) and consider provisioning a short-lived dedicated pool for acme.
- We'll collect a short trace bundle and upload to the incident playbook link.

I'll continue to update every 10 minutes. Requesting Priyom to confirm messaging to customer and Marcus to sign off on emergency spend if needed.

Soojin
Sr. SRE, Inference Operations
